choice: Changed GraphQL `mlflowSearchModelVersions` filtering to use the same prompt-aware check as REST (`_rm_or_prompt_read_predicate`), because it only checked registered-model permissions and let users without prompt access read prompt templates over GraphQL.
final:
I fixed an access-control gap in GraphQL that let users read prompt contents they don't have permission to see.

**The problem:** GraphQL's `mlflowSearchModelVersions` checked every result against the user's registered-model permissions only (`mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py`, in `GraphQLAuthorizationMiddleware._filter_model_versions_result`). In MLflow, prompts are stored as registered models, but they have their own separate permissions. The REST search endpoint checks the prompt permissions for prompt versions; GraphQL didn't. So a user who could read registered models but had no prompt access could query a prompt version over `/graphql` and get its tags, which hold the full prompt template text. The reverse was also wrong: a user who did have prompt access could have their prompt versions wrongly hidden.

**The fix:** the GraphQL filter now uses `_rm_or_prompt_read_predicate`, the same check the REST endpoint uses. It looks at the `mlflow.prompt.is_prompt` tag on each result and checks prompt permissions for prompts and registered-model permissions for everything else.

**Tests:** I couldn't run the command exactly as you gave it. A local hook blocks bare `python3` and asks for `uv run python`, and plain `uv run` failed because it couldn't download a Python interpreter (no network). So I ran the same five test files through `uv run` with the repo's existing Python environment: **453 passed**. I didn't add a regression test for the GraphQL prompt case, so none of those tests exercises the bug directly.

**Another gap I didn't fix:** the nested `modelVersions` field on GraphQL runs (`MlflowRunExtension.resolve_model_versions`) isn't filtered at all. Anyone who can read a run can see the model versions registered from it, even for registered models they can't read. That exposes less than the prompt bug did, so I picked the prompt bug and left this one alone. It's worth a follow-up.

CHOICE: Changed GraphQL `mlflowSearchModelVersions` filtering to use the same prompt-aware check as REST (`_rm_or_prompt_read_predicate`), because it only checked registered-model permissions and let users without prompt access read prompt templates over GraphQL.
